title: Relative ampleness is open on the base
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. If $x\in X$ and the restriction $\mathcal M|_{Y_x}$ to the fibre [def-pc-fibre-product] is ample in the absolute sense of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ in $X$ such that $f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact and $\mathcal M|_{f^{-1}(U)}$ is ample on every inverse image of an affine open of $U$ (that is, it is relatively ample over $U$ in the stated sense).

mathlib_searches.query: proper morphism invertible sheaf ample on fibre implies relatively ample on an open neighbourhood of the base point
mathlib_searches.results: hits concern proper morphism locality and affine neighborhoods; no ampleness theorem

mathlib_searches.query: ampleness in a neighbourhood for a proper morphism
mathlib_searches.results: generic IsProper and locally finite type declarations; no ampleness result

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding.
